target_customer: Consumers on iPhone looking for restaurant recommendations; no paying customer identified
problem: Restaurant reviews on sites like Yelp were long and slow to write, so the founders offered thumbs up or down votes and short comments with a points game layered on top.
business_model: Free consumer app and website; no revenue model found in sources
product_category: Location based restaurant reviews with game mechanics

founders.name: Nikhil Pandit
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder with no background given

founders.name: Jared Tame
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder with no background given

competitors.name: Yelp
competitors.what: Established local review site with an iPhone app
competitors.traction_then: Large volume of reviews; TechCrunch called it a very tough competitor

competitors.name: Foursquare
competitors.what: Location check-in service rewarding check-ins with points

competitors.name: CrashCorp
competitors.what: Mobile startup working on location and augmented reality for the iPhone (Crash Corp founded May 2009 by Joe Stump and Matt Galligan, per TechCrunch)
competitors.traction_then: Not established; TechCrunch mentions it only as a link on other AR apps on the way

technical_complexity.rationale: A web service plus an iPhone app with votes, points and territory tied to city blocks; a two person team shipped it within one batch. An AR app was only shown as a demo video.

defensibility.rationale: Short reviews and a points game were easy to copy and the product had no stated network or data advantage at launch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Neither copied it as far as the sources show; Loopt, another YC company, bought it in October 2009 a few months after the August launch.

market_need_then: Mobile local discovery was hot in 2009 with Foursquare and Gowalla growing and Yelp's iPhone app active; the founders argued long reviews did not fit the Twitter era.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful gang and street metaphors (mobs, territory, street cred) per the product description

brand_strength.rationale: Only a few months of public life and press coverage was about the product, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: GraffitiGeo launched in August 2009 as a thumbs up or down restaurant review app with a territory game, and Loopt, a fellow YC company, acquired it in October 2009 for undisclosed terms. With almost no disclosed funding and only months of public life, the sale looks like a quick team and product pickup rather than a proven business, but no source states the deal's rationale or what became of the app.
notes: Company site not provided in the directory and no live site found. Databases list about 20K from YC (CB Insights, Seedtable) and Dealroom lists a 500 to 750K value; these are aggregator figures, unverified, and not recorded as rounds. The acquisition rationale beyond Loopt's purchase was not found; whether the product shut down is not public in sources seen. Founder backgrounds not found. Audit fix: the 20K from Y Combinator is recorded as a round; it rests on databases (CB Insights, Seedtable and Dealroom agree on 20K) and no primary source, and the Dealroom 500 to 750K value is not recorded. CrashCorp is added as a competitor: the TechCrunch article of 2009-08-13 links to it on the words 'other AR apps' but does not name it in the text, and a TechCrunch post of 2009-05-16 covers its founding.
